originality.rationale: The cited primary paper gives empirical class counts and degree-conditioned typical vertex moments, not temporal mixed-normal fluctuations of fixed-birth old hubs. Published uniform half-degree concentration gives a weaker upper bound without the sharp Gaussian law. Global-leaf covariance results track another variable and do not imply the local mixed CLT. An inaccessible plausible stronger source remains a material priority risk.

value.rationale: Identifies an explicit sharp second-order and cross-hub fluctuation law at the natural fourth-root size scale. Unlike empirical high-degree tables, it resolves random old-hub growth effects and proves independent Gaussian noise upon observable-degree normalization, a natural fluctuation invariant not implied by existing global class-count theory.
